# Native memory paired A/B: Orion memory on vs. off

**Status:** recorded result, reproducible from this repository
**Recorded run:** `20261003T213755Z-ab-fae54b` (2026-10-03, 21:37–21:44 UTC)
**Implementation revision:** `9ebb73034c10f123e31ee9222ea82464d32967b5`
**Version line:** `v0.00.07` Helix (Stage 151–160) with the v1 service chain
**Generated by:** [scripts/memory_ab.py](scripts/memory_ab.py)
**Raw data:** [data/memory-on-off-ab-recorded.json](data/memory-on-off-ab-recorded.json)

## 1. Question

Does retrieving Civilization's native (Orion) memory change answers on a fixed
task, compared with the *same* model on the *same* questions with memory
retrieval switched off?

This is a controlled comparison of one deployment against itself. It is not a
comparison of Civilization against another model or another system.

## 2. Design

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Conditions | `memory_on` (`read_memory = true`) vs. `memory_off` (`read_memory = false`) |
| Held constant | question text, option set and order, task name, session memory contents, provider model, seed |
| Only difference | `CivilizationRequest.read_memory` |
| Automatic writing | disabled in both conditions (`write_memory = false`), so the answer key stays fixed |
| Repetition | 3 rounds over the same 25 questions → 75 paired observations (63 answerable) |
| Order control | condition order alternates by case index and round |
| Isolation | each round uses fresh sessions; the negative-control cases write to a separate source session |
| Scoring | exact match against a synthetic answer key; no LLM judge |

**What "memory on" actually does.** With `read_memory = true` the service
retrieves the top matching cells from the session store and injects them into
the ordinary prediction context before the decision is made. The response
carries an Orion trace (`retrieved_cell_ids`, `injected_item_count`), so memory
*use* is verified from the trace rather than inferred from the answer.

**Materials.** 25 synthetic four-choice questions across six axes: atomic fact
recall (5), preference recall (4), temporal ordering (4), similar-entity
interference (4), knowledge update (4), and session isolation plus abstention
(4). 33 memory records are written per round; the run configuration retrieves
at most 4 cells, injects at most 4, and truncates each to 512 characters.
Current retrieval is a lexical scoring path over term overlap, memory system,
importance, confidence, and link score — vector retrieval is not part of this
deployment and is therefore not claimed here.

## 3. Results

### 3.1 Headline

| Metric | memory_on | memory_off | Difference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| All questions, including abstention controls | 75/75 (100%) | 29/75 (38.7%) | +61.3 pp |
| Answerable questions | 63/63 (100%) | 17/63 (27.0%) | **+73.0 pp** |
| Isolation / abstention negative controls | 12/12 (100%) | 12/12 (100%) | none |
| Requests with an API error | 0/75 | 0/75 | none |
| Target memory present in the prediction context | 63/63 (100%) | 0/63 (0%) | as designed |

### 3.2 Paired outcomes

| Paired outcome | Pairs |
|---|---:|
| Both conditions correct | 29 |
| Only `memory_on` correct | **46** |
| Only `memory_off` correct | **0** |
| Both conditions wrong | 0 |
| Total pairs | 75 |

The paired view is the reason to trust this result more than the raw delta:
memory retrieval converted 46 wrong answers into correct ones, and in no pair
did enabling memory turn a correct answer into a wrong one.

### 3.3 By question axis

| Axis | Unique questions | memory_on correct | memory_off correct | Wins unique to memory_on |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Atomic fact recall | 5 | 15/15 | 3/15 | 12 |
| Preference recall | 4 | 12/12 | 3/12 | 9 |
| Temporal ordering | 4 | 12/12 | 1/12 | 11 |
| Similar-entity interference | 4 | 12/12 | 4/12 | 8 |
| Knowledge update | 4 | 12/12 | 6/12 | 6 |
| Session isolation and abstention | 4 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 0 |

The largest effects appear where the question cannot be answered from its own
wording: temporal ordering, atomic fact recall, preference recall, and
disambiguation between similar entities. Knowledge update is the smallest
effect because the memory-off condition already answered half of those items
correctly by guessing.

### 3.4 Latency (observed, not a throughput claim)

| Condition | Mean | P50 | P95 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| memory_on | 1,846.5 ms | 1,804.8 ms | 2,565.1 ms |
| memory_off | 3,585.8 ms | 3,188.6 ms | 6,745.7 ms |

Latency here is end-to-end through the local service and the model gateway, on
one machine, with fixed options. Generation length and provider-side variance
dominate, so this is not evidence that the memory path improves throughput.

## 4. Supporting tracks (context, different protocols)

The same evaluation campaign also ran public benchmarks through a local adapter
that bridges the benchmark memory client to the Orion memory API. Those tracks
did **not** include a memory-off paired baseline, so they cannot be used to
claim a memory gain; they are reported as positioning data.

| Track | Sample | Top-10 | Top-20 | API errors |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| LongMemEval (two stratified seeds, merged) | 12 questions, 2 per category | 8/12 (66.7%) | 9/12 (75.0%) | 0 |
| BEAM 100K | 20 questions, 2 per category, 94 memories written | 13/20 (65.0%) | 15/20 (75.0%) | 0 |
| BEAM 500K | 6 questions, 3 categories, 398 memories written | 5/6 (83.3%) | 5/6 (83.3%) | 0 |
| BEAM 1M | 6 questions, 3 categories, 855 memories written | 2/6 (33.3%) | 2/6 (33.3%) | 0 |

Known weak spots, reported as error-location signals rather than stable scores
(each cell is 2 questions): LongMemEval preference questions 0/2; BEAM 1M
temporal reasoning 0/2, and the same three categories fell from 5/6 at 500K to
2/6 at 1M. Long-context behaviour needs more seeds, more conversation indices,
and more items per category before any trend is called stable.

A separate single-condition track used the native API directly (no benchmark
answerer or judge): 25/25 exact matches, the target memory inside the Top-4 for
21/21 answerable questions, rank 1 for 16/21 (MRR 0.881), 4/4 isolation cases
with no cross-session leakage, 4/4 correct abstentions, and 0 API errors.

## 5. Threats to validity

1. **25 unique questions, not 75.** The three rounds measure repeatability of
   the same items; they do not widen the question sample.
2. **Synthetic fixed-choice items.** Questions use synthetic facts and four
   options; option wording can carry signal, and the memory-off condition is
   allowed to guess. Read the paired wins and losses, not the headline delta
   alone.
3. **Session scope only.** Retrieval here comes from the session store of the
   same running process. Process-restart persistence, global-store save/load,
   cross-user sharing, concurrency, working-memory expiry, procedural memory,
   and automatic extraction from free text are outside this experiment.
4. **Not a benchmark comparison.** LongMemEval and BEAM use their own answerers
   and judges; this A/B uses a fixed answer key. A high score on the synthetic
   set is not evidence of superiority on public benchmarks.
5. **Deployment-specific retrieval.** The measured behaviour reflects this
   service configuration (Top-4 lexical retrieval, 4 injected cells, 512
   characters each). A different configuration is a different experiment.

## 6. Reproducing

The reproduction script is self-contained: it embeds the 25 question fixtures
and needs only a reachable service and the `civilization_v1` SDK.

```bash
cd docs/versions/v0.00.07-helix/experiments/scripts

# full protocol: 3 rounds, 25 questions, 150 predictions
CIVILIZATION_LOCAL_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765 \
  python memory_ab.py --rounds 3 --provider-model <model-name> --output memory_on_vs_off.json

# smoke run: 1 round, first 4 questions
python memory_ab.py --rounds 1 --max-cases 4 --output smoke.json
```

The script refuses to run unless the service reports ready, writes each run into
fresh sessions named after its run id, and records per-question predictions,
retrieval ranks, injected cell ids, latencies, and errors in the result JSON.

**Verification performed for this publication:** the embedded script was run
against a live service as a 1-round / 3-question smoke test and produced
3/3 correct with memory on, 0/3 with memory off, 0 API errors, and the expected
paired structure. The recorded result in `data/` is the full 3-round run listed
at the top of this document.

## 7. What this experiment does and does not show

**Shows:** in this controlled, single-deployment, 25-item synthetic task set,
reading Civilization's native memory improves decision accuracy substantially
(+46 paired wins, 0 paired losses), and the memory service behaved as designed
(target cells injected whenever memory was on, never leaked across the isolated
session boundary, no API errors).

**Does not show:** general superiority over other memory systems or models,
long-term or cross-restart memory behaviour, free-form conversation quality, or
a throughput benefit.
